analysis:
This PR changes CI plumbing only: .git, SwiftPM and build caches, sparse checkouts, a mimo_audio component output, a CMake tool-cache shortcut, and docs. It touches no provider runtime code, coordinator contract or key material. None of the retained threats (T-041 and the TB-002/003/007/009/011/012/013 set) is altered, and T-041's prefix-cache text is not affected.

Cache poisoning: ci.yml sets SAVE_CACHES only for push events on master or dev. Every save step is gated on it (ci.yml 694, 897, 960-965, 1033, 1095, 1153). Pull requests, including forks, only restore caches. Restored .git, SwiftPM and build caches therefore come from trusted branch pushes, and a PR cannot plant a cache for later runs. The restore-keys fall back to prefix matches, but only trusted pushes write those keys.

Restored .git is validated with git rev-parse and git fsck --connectivity-only (ci.yml 682-686). That check does not verify hooks or config. This is acceptable because only master/dev pushes save it, and persist-credentials: false keeps the job token out of the cached .git/config.

The docs-impact checkout (docs-impact.yml 57-68) uses the pull_request event and the PR head SHA with contents: read. The sparse-checkout and blob:none filter change what is fetched, not privileges.

Not verified: scripts/install-release-cmake.sh, which is not supplied. Per build.md it reuses the image's tool-cache CMake when a marker file exists and the binary reports version 3.31.12. That trusts the runner image and does not re-checksum the binary. The doc says release and signing jobs keep literal Blacksmith labels, but whether release builds use this path was not checked.

Also not in view: the provider-ci-build composite action and the first half of ci.yml, which is truncated, so I could not confirm that release jobs do not restore PR-influenced caches. The mimo_audio path-conditioned gate reduces CI coverage on unrelated PRs; that is a quality tradeoff, not a security regression. No security finding is raised.
